host_prefix.description: An IPv4 CIDR range used to allocate host addresses when booting compute into a VPC. For SUNK clusters, use a prefix no smaller than your Zone's default host prefix (a mask no longer than the default) so that host addresses reflect each node's physical location. SUNK uses this location information to place network-adjacent nodes together, which improves distributed-training performance. A prefix smaller than the Zone default (a longer mask) doesn't carry this location information, so it produces less optimal placement. If you need a different size, CoreWeave can approve one for your account on request. For non-SUNK VPCs, any prefix size is accepted. However, NVL72 rack-level instances require a host prefix no smaller than the Zone's default host prefix. A smaller prefix forces dynamic address allocation, which breaks standard IMEX address mapping across the cluster. IMEX with Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) doesn't have this limitation. If left unspecified, a Zone-specific default value will be applied by the server. See [Host prefixes](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/networking/vpc/create-manage-vpcs#host-prefixes) for details. This field is immutable once set.

host_prefixes.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR ranges used to allocate host addresses when booting compute into a VPC. For SUNK clusters, use an IPv4 prefix no smaller than your Zone's default host prefix (a mask no longer than the default) so that host addresses reflect each node's physical location. SUNK uses this location information to place network-adjacent nodes together, which improves distributed-training performance. A prefix smaller than the Zone default (a longer mask) doesn't carry this location information, so it produces less optimal placement. If you need a different size, CoreWeave can approve one for your account on request. For non-SUNK VPCs, any prefix size is accepted. However, NVL72 rack-level instances require a primary host prefix (`type = PRIMARY`) no smaller than the Zone's default host prefix. A smaller prefix forces dynamic address allocation, which breaks standard IMEX address mapping across the cluster. IMEX with Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) doesn't have this limitation. See [Host prefixes](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/networking/vpc/create-manage-vpcs#host-prefixes) for details.

attributes.description: Creation attributes, at most 15 entries. Keys must be lowercase DNS labels of 1–63 characters and must not start with cw-, role, or groups. Values must be Kubernetes label values of at most 63 characters (empty allowed). Changes replace the key. Omitted values are adopted during import.

duration_seconds.description: Required for creation; integer from 0 to 4294967295. Zero means permanent. Omit only when retaining an imported key whose original duration is unavailable. Changing this value replaces the key.

expiry.description: Expiry in RFC 3339 UTC format, or null for a permanent key (including an absent or year-one API expiry).

id.description: Access-key ID. Used for import and individual revocation.

org_id.description: Organization cloud ID reported by the API.

principal_name.description: Principal determined by the authenticated caller.

secret_key.description: Secret returned only at creation. Preserved during refresh; unavailable after import. Sensitive values remain in Terraform state and state backups.

status.description: Read-only API status, such as ACTIVE, EXPIRED, or FULL_SUSPENDED. The provider never changes principal-wide status.

block.description:
Manages one AI Object Storage access key for the authenticated caller. Existing organization policies determine its permissions. Destroy revokes only this key.

Set `duration_seconds` explicitly when creating a key: zero creates a permanent key. Changes to duration or attributes replace the key. Use `terraform apply -replace=coreweave_object_storage_access_key.example` for manual rotation. There is no background renewal; distribute the new secret to consumers before removing an old key, using separate resources when an overlap is needed.

Refresh removes missing keys and keys reported as `DELETED` from state, so the next apply recreates them when a duration is configured. Expired and inactive keys remain managed, with their API status and a warning; they are not automatically rotated or reactivated. If the service later removes an expired key, it is treated as missing.

Import uses the key ID. The secret and original duration cannot be recovered and remain null. Omit `duration_seconds` in the imported resource configuration to keep the existing key; setting it explicitly plans replacement. Omit attributes to adopt the imported values, or configure the same values. Supply an explicit duration before intentionally replacing an imported key.

Protect access to Terraform state and backups: marking the secret sensitive hides normal CLI output but does not encrypt or omit it from state. Key creation is sent once without automatic retries. If its response is lost, a key may exist whose ID and secret were not saved; inspect keys using the service tooling before trying again.

name.description: The bucket name. Must be globally unique and must not begin with `cw-` or `vip-`.

tags.description: Map of tags to assign to the bucket.

block.description: Buckets are the primary organizational containers for your data in CoreWeave AI Object Storage. Bucket names must be globally-unique and not begin with `cw-` or `vip-`, which are reserved for internal use. Before creation, the provider verifies the complete list of buckets owned by the organization and fails without sending a create request if that inventory cannot be completed; an existing bucket with the requested name must be imported. Learn more about [creating buckets](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/buckets/create-bucket).

bucket.description: Name of source bucket to which the inventory configuration applies

enabled.description: Whether the inventory configuration is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

included_object_versions.description: Object versions to include: `All` includes all versions; `Current` includes only current versions.

optional_fields.description: Additional report fields: `Size`, `LastModifiedDate`, `LastAccessedDate`, `StorageClass`, `ETag`, `IsMultipartUploaded`, `EncryptionStatus`, `ChecksumAlgorithm`. Omit to include no additional fields; an empty set is invalid.

account_id.description: Account ID of the destination bucket owner.

prefix.description: Prefix prepended to the report output path.

block.description: Required. Destination bucket for the report (may equal the source bucket).

Required. Where the inventory report is written. May be the same bucket as the source. The destination policy must grant the inventory service `s3:PutObject` and `s3:AbortMultipartUpload` on report objects. Use `depends_on` to apply that policy before the inventory configuration. Bucket policies are evaluated after organization policies; requests without a matching bucket grant are implicitly denied even if an organization policy allows them. Include caller permissions for Terraform bucket reads and cleanup, and explicit grants for report readers. The policy resource replaces the entire existing bucket policy, so retain all required statements. `s3:PutBucketPolicy` itself evaluates organization permissions only. See [policy evaluation](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/policies#policy-evaluation).
Limits the inventory report to objects matching a prefix.

frequency.description: How frequently the report is generated: `Daily` or `Weekly`.

block.description: Required. Schedule for generating the inventory report.

Manages a CoreWeave AI Object Storage bucket inventory configuration. The provider obtains temporary S3 credentials using its configured authentication; no separately managed access-key resource is required. The authenticated identity must have permission to manage inventory configurations on the source bucket and policies on the destination bucket. [Learn more about inventory reporting](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/buckets/inventory-reporting/configure).

bucket.description: Name of the bucket to apply lifecycle configuration to

prefix.description: Deprecated. Object key prefix to which the rule applies. CoreWeave AI Object Storage rejects requests that set this field; use `filter.prefix` instead.

object_size_greater_than.description: Minimum object size (in bytes) to which the rule applies.

object_size_less_than.description: Maximum object size (in bytes) to which the rule applies.

object_size_greater_than.description: Minimum object size (in bytes) to which the rule applies.

object_size_less_than.description: Maximum object size (in bytes) to which the rule applies.

tags.description: Map for specifying tag keys and values.

block.description: Configuration block used to apply a logical AND to two or more predicates. The Lifecycle Rule will apply to any object matching all the predicates configured inside the and block.

newer_noncurrent_versions.description: Number of noncurrent versions to retain

days.description: Number of days after object creation for transition

block.description: One or more lifecycle rule blocks

Lifecycle configurations automate object management by defining actions applied to objects over time, such as expiring objects after a specified period or transitioning them to different storage tiers. This helps optimize storage costs and maintain data hygiene. [Learn more about S3-compatible lifecycle bucket configurations](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/reference/object-storage-s3#bucket-lifecycles).

bucket.description: The name of the bucket for which to apply this policy.

policy.description: Text of the policy. Must be valid JSON. The coreweave_object_storage_bucket_policy_document data source may be used, simply reference the `.json` attribute of the data source.

block.description: [Bucket access policies](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/bucket-access/bucket-policies) allow you to define precise, S3-compatible access control for one bucket. These are optional, and are evaluated after organization access policies. See [Manage Bucket Policies](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/bucket-access/manage-bucket-policies#example-policies) for examples and further information.

archive_after_last_access_days.description: Days since last access (or creation if never accessed) before a STANDARD object version is archived to STANDARD_IA. The default minimum is 60; your organization's entitlement may permit a different minimum, so the effective floor is validated server-side. Required when `archive_enabled` is true, and rejected otherwise.

archive_enabled.description: When true, idle STANDARD objects are archived to STANDARD_IA after `archive_after_last_access_days` without access. Your organization must be entitled to configure this setting.

audit_logging_enabled.description: Whether audit logging is enabled for the bucket. Contact support to enable audit logging for your organization before enabling this setting.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to manage settings for.

block.description: Manage settings for a CoreWeave AI Object Storage bucket.

bucket.description: The bucket on which to enable or suspend versioning.

status.description: Versioning state of the bucket. Valid values: Enabled, Suspended, or Disabled. Disabled should only be used when creating or importing resources that correspond to unversioned S3 buckets since the S3 API does not allow setting an Enabled/Suspended bucket to Disabled.

block.description: Versioning protects your data by preserving all versions of objects and preventing permanent deletion. When objects are deleted, they are "soft deleted" with delete markers, allowing you to restore previous versions and recover data. After creating a versioned bucket with Terraform, [use `rclone` to manage versioned objects and delete markers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/buckets/rclone-versioned-buckets).

name.description: The name of the organization access policy, must be unique.

actions.description: Defines which operations the policy allows or denies. Organization access policies can include actions from two APIs - S3 (s3:*) and AI Object Storage API (cwobject:*). You can use wildcards (like s3:* or cwobject:*) to cover multiple actions at once.

effect.description: Must be either Allow or Deny (case-sensitive). Determines whether the statement grants or denies the specified actions on the listed resources for the designated principals. By default, all access is denied.

name.description: A short, human-readable identifier for this specific policy statement, similar to Sid in bucket access policies.

principals.description: Defines which users, roles, or groups the policy applies to. Only short-form identifiers are supported. If you use a full ARN, the policy will fail with an error. See the [AI Object Storage documentation](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/organization-policies/about) for guidelines on defining principals.

resources.description: Defines which resources the policy applies to. See the [AI Object Storage documentation](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/organization-policies/about) for guidelines on defining resources.

statements.description: The list of access policy statements associated with this policy. At least one statement is required.

block.description: [Organization access policies](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/organization-policies/about) enforce permissions for AI Object Storage across your entire CoreWeave organization, automatically covering every resource, bucket, and user in your account. At least one organization access policy must be in place before you can create a bucket.

cluster_id.description: CKS cluster UUID. Changing it replaces the runner.

cluster_name.description: Cluster display name resolved by the server.

data_plane_status.description: Observed direct endpoint state, URI, protocols, and certificate expiry as JSON, or null.

deployment_spec.description: Resolved deployment configuration as JSON. Read-only; use spec.overrides to change supported settings.

etag.description: Opaque policy revision used for optimistic concurrency. A concurrent policy edit fails the apply; refresh the plan before retrying.

id.description: Terraform resource ID, equal to runner_id within the authenticated organization.

install_error.description: Structured installation failure details as JSON, or null.

base.description: Runtime defaults and attachments as a JSON object, for example `jsonencode({ ... })`. Typed constraints belong in constraints. Values are stored in Terraform state.

allowed_images.description: Allowed image references. Empty permits any image within the registry restrictions.

allowed_registries.description: Allowed registry prefixes. Empty permits any registry.

allowed_instance_types.description: Allowed instance types. Empty permits any offered by the runner.

default_lifetime_seconds.description: Default sandbox lifetime in seconds; zero leaves the platform default. Maximum 30 days.

max_annotation_count.description: Maximum annotations; zero means no limit.

any.description: Set to true to select any address-shaped peer.

dns_name.description: Exact DNS name or a single leftmost wildcard label; `*` is allowed only in allowed_egress.

dns_name_except.description: DNS names excluded from an allowed_egress DNS envelope.

end_port.description: Inclusive end port; zero or omitted means a single port.

ports.description: Allowed ports. Empty means all ports, except DNS destinations which use HTTPS (TCP 443).

namespace_labels.description: Namespace labels to match. Omitted means the sandbox's own namespace.

pod_labels.description: Pod labels to match (at least one required).

selector.description: Explicit entitlement to reach cluster workloads by label.

allowed_egress.description: Allowed egress envelope. DNS wildcard `*` is permitted here. Select exactly one peer kind per rule.

any.description: Set to true to select any address-shaped peer.

end_port.description: Inclusive end port; zero or omitted means a single port.

ports.description: Allowed ports. Empty means all ports, except DNS destinations which use HTTPS (TCP 443).

allowed_ingress.description: Allowed ingress sources for custom-visibility ports. Select exactly one peer kind per rule.

any.description: Set to true to select any address-shaped peer.

dns_name.description: Exact DNS name or a single leftmost wildcard label; `*` is allowed only in allowed_egress.

dns_name_except.description: DNS names excluded from an allowed_egress DNS envelope.

end_port.description: Inclusive end port; zero or omitted means a single port.

ports.description: Allowed ports. Empty means all ports, except DNS destinations which use HTTPS (TCP 443).

namespace_labels.description: Namespace labels to match. Omitted means the sandbox's own namespace.

pod_labels.description: Pod labels to match (at least one required).

selector.description: Explicit entitlement to reach cluster workloads by label.

default_egress.description: Egress applied when the sandbox specifies none. DNS-name destinations are not permitted here. Select exactly one peer kind per rule.

any.description: Set to true to select any address-shaped peer.

end_port.description: Inclusive end port; zero or omitted means a single port.

ports.description: Allowed ports. Empty means all ports, except DNS destinations which use HTTPS (TCP 443).

default_ingress.description: Ingress applied when the sandbox specifies none. Select exactly one peer kind per rule.

deny_dns.description: Forbid DNS-name egress grants. Does not disable DNS resolution.

network.description: Network envelopes and defaults. Empty allowed envelopes impose no restriction.

cpu_ceiling.description: Sum-of-requests CPU ceiling across the sandbox.

max_cpu.description: Maximum CPU per container, as a Kubernetes quantity.

max_gpu_count.description: Maximum GPUs per container. Omitted means no cap; explicit zero forbids GPUs.

memory_ceiling.description: Sum-of-requests memory ceiling across the sandbox.

require_limits.description: Require every container to declare requests and limits.

resources.description: Per-container bounds, defaults, and whole-sandbox ceilings.

allowed_capabilities.description: Linux capabilities containers may add. Empty permits none beyond defaults.

allowed_runtime_classes.description: Runtime classes callers may explicitly select. Empty forbids caller-selected runtime classes.

allowed_seccomp_profiles.description: Permitted seccomp profiles, such as RuntimeDefault or Unconfined.

default_cpu_runtime_class.description: Default CPU runtime class. Must fit a nonempty runtime-class allowlist.

default_gpu_runtime_class.description: Default GPU runtime class. Must fit a nonempty runtime-class allowlist.

allowed_media.description: Allowed storage media. Empty permits any.

max_size.description: Maximum size per volume, for example 100Gi.

constraints.description: Typed constraints applied to the resolved sandbox specification. Omitted groups impose no constraint of that kind; individual security allowlists remain fail-closed.

cidrs.description: Canonical, nonredundant IPv4/IPv6 prefixes (at most 256). Do not include a prefix already covered by another entry. An empty set denies every public source. Omitting the enclosing source_ip_allowlist leaves access unrestricted.

source_ip_allowlist.description: Public source IP restriction. A present empty object denies every public source; an absent object imposes no source IP restriction.

control_plane_access.description: Request-time controls in addition to authentication and tenant authorization.

policy.description: Policy governing every sandbox on this runner. Required even for the explicit empty posture `policy = {}`. Policy is updated with an etag to detect concurrent changes.

rollout_in_progress.description: Whether a newer desired revision is still rolling out.

runner_group_id.description: Runner group for scheduling affinity. Defaults to `default`; omitting or setting this attribute to null resets a custom group to `default`.

runner_id.description: Operator-assigned runner identifier, unique within the authenticated organization. Changing it replaces the runner.

advertised_uri.description: Stable absolute URI returned to direct clients.

service_annotations.description: Annotations on the backing ClusterIP service.

disabled.description: Set to true to explicitly disable the direct endpoint.

hostname.description: Endpoint DNS name included in the server certificate. The platform may assign one when empty.

load_balancer.description: Expose through an L4 load balancer forwarding mutual TLS to the runner.

data_plane.description: Direct sandbox data endpoint. Select exactly one of disabled, cluster_ip, load_balancer, or custom. Certificates are managed by the platform.

enforce_resource_limits.description: Require sandboxes to declare both memory and CPU limits.

policy.description: Image pull policy. The platform default is IF_NOT_PRESENT. ALWAYS reauthorizes pull credentials on every start. Values: `SANDBOX_IMAGE_PULL_POLICY_IF_NOT_PRESENT`, `SANDBOX_IMAGE_PULL_POLICY_ALWAYS`.

end_time.description: Exclusive RFC 3339 end timestamp, after start_time.

exclusions.description: One-time periods during which updates cannot start.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression in UTC, for example `0 2 * * SAT`.

windows.description: Recurring update windows. An empty list permits updates at any time outside exclusions.

maintenance_policy.description: Update scheduling in UTC. Exclusions take precedence over windows.

env.description: Runner environment overrides. Values are stored in Terraform state; use a protected state backend.

node_selector.description: Node label selectors for the runner deployment.

resources.description: CPU and memory requests and limits for runner pods, as Kubernetes quantities.

replicas.description: Desired replicas when autoscaling is disabled.

effect.description: Taint effect. Empty matches all effects.

release_channel.description: Automatic update channel. Defaults to stable. Values: `RELEASE_CHANNEL_STABLE`, `RELEASE_CHANNEL_RAPID`.

image.description: Release-pinned collector image. Empty retains the deployment environment's image.

tenant_metrics.description: Per-sandbox tenant usage collection. Overrides corresponding deployment environment entries.

csi_driver_allowlist.description: Allowed CSI drivers. Empty uses the platform default (`csi.vastdata.com`).

enabled.description: Enable registered volume mounts; the runner's PVC/PV permission preflight must also pass.

volumes.description: Registered volume support. These settings take precedence over corresponding deployment environment entries.

spec.description: Desired runner configuration. When omitted, the server's defaults are adopted. Removing an optional setting inside this object resets that setting through an explicit update mask.

update_available.description: Whether a newer version is available on the release channel.

zone.description: Lowercase geographic zone of the runner, for example `us-east-04a`. Use `lower(coreweave_cks_cluster.example.zone)` when referencing a CKS cluster zone. Changing it replaces the runner.

block.description: Manages a CoreWeave Sandbox runner and its required policy through the v1 RunnerManagementService (`/v1/sandbox/managedRunners`). Requires a server implementing full v1 managed-runner CRUD; the policy-only v1 server cannot provision or fully refresh this resource. Creation and updates record the accepted desired configuration; installation and rollout continue asynchronously and are exposed in computed status attributes. Deletion waits up to 30 minutes for the runner to disappear.

active.description: Whether tokens issued by this OIDC provider are accepted for workload identity federation. Defaults to `true` when omitted on creation. Once a value has been applied it is retained: removing the attribute from configuration keeps the last applied value rather than reverting to `true`, so a configuration that was deactivated stays deactivated. Set `active = true` explicitly to reactivate one.

audience.description: The expected audience claim in tokens issued by the external OIDC provider.

created_at.description: The RFC 3339 timestamp at which the OIDC configuration was created.

deactivated_at.description: The RFC 3339 timestamp at which the OIDC configuration was deactivated, or null while it is active.

description.description: An optional human-readable description of the OIDC configuration.

id.description: The server-assigned unique identifier for the OIDC configuration.

issuer_url.description: The issuer URL of the external OIDC provider. HTTPS is required except for loopback development issuers.

name.description: A human-readable name for the OIDC configuration. Must contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.

organization_id.description: The unique identifier of the CoreWeave organization that owns the OIDC configuration.

updated_at.description: The RFC 3339 timestamp at which the OIDC configuration was last updated.

block.description: Creates and manages an external OpenID Connect (OIDC) trust configuration for CoreWeave workload identity federation.

organization_id.description: The unique identifier of the organization associated with the configured CoreWeave API token.

principal_id.description: The unique identifier of the principal associated with the configured CoreWeave API token.

block.description:
Retrieve the organization and principal identifiers associated with the configured CoreWeave API token.

Comparable identity data sources in other HashiCorp cloud providers include [aws_caller_identity](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/data-sources/caller_identity), [azurerm_client_config](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/data-sources/client_config), and [google_client_openid_userinfo](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/data-sources/client_openid_userinfo). Each data source reflects its provider's identity model and exports different attributes.

block.description: The main policy element that defines the access rules for buckets and objects. Multiple statement blocks can be specified.

[Bucket access policies](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/bucket-access/bucket-policies) allow you to define precise, S3-compatible access control for one bucket. They are evaluated after organization access policies. See [Manage Bucket Policies](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/storage/object-storage/auth-access/bucket-access/manage-bucket-policies#example-policies) for examples and further information. This data source provides a type-safe data structure for creating an S3-compatible JSON bucket policy.
